Work: Fill in the blanks:
1) $3 \times 3 \times 3 \times 3 = 3^{\square}$
2) $5^{\square} \times 5^3 = 5^5$
3) $a^2 \times a^{\square} = a^{-3}$
4) $(-5)^0 = \square$
5) $\frac{4}{4^{\square}} = 1$

We observe, $5^{\frac{1}{2}} \times 5^{\frac{1}{2}} = (5^{\frac{1}{2}})^2$

Again, $5^{\frac{1}{2}} \times 5^{\frac{1}{2}} = 5^{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}} = 5^{2 \times \frac{1}{2}} = 5$

$\therefore (5^{\frac{1}{2}})^2 = 5$

Square (power 2) of $(5^{\frac{1}{2}}) = 5$ and square root (second root) of $5 = 5^{\frac{1}{2}}$

$5^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is written as $\sqrt{5}$.

Again we observe, $5^{\frac{1}{3}} \times 5^{\frac{1}{3}} \times 5^{\frac{1}{3}} = (5^{\frac{1}{3}})^3$

Again, $5^{\frac{1}{3}} \times 5^{\frac{1}{3}} \times 5^{\frac{1}{3}} = 5^{\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}} = 5^{3 \times \frac{1}{3}} = 5$

Cube (power 3) of $5^{\frac{1}{3}} = 5$ and cube root (third root) of $5 = 5^{\frac{1}{3}}$

$5^{\frac{1}{3}}$ is written as $\sqrt[3]{5}$.

In the case of $n$ th root,

$a^{\frac{1}{n}} \times a^{\frac{1}{n}} \times a^{\frac{1}{n}} \times \dots \times a^{\frac{1}{n}}$ [successive multiplication of $n$ $a^{\frac{1}{n}}$'s] $= (a^{\frac{1}{n}})^n$

Again, $a^{\frac{1}{n}} \times a^{\frac{1}{n}} \times a^{\frac{1}{n}} \times \dots \times a^{\frac{1}{n}}$

$= a^{\frac{1}{n}+\frac{1}{n}+\frac{1}{n}+\dots+\frac{1}{n}}$ [in the exponent, sum of $n$ $\frac{1}{n}$'s]

$= a^{n \times \frac{1}{n}} = a$

$\therefore (a^{\frac{1}{n}})^n = a$

The $n$ th power of $a^{\frac{1}{n}}$ is $a$ and the $n$ th root of $a$ is $a^{\frac{1}{n}}$

i.e, $n$ th power of $a^{\frac{1}{n}}$ is $(a^{\frac{1}{n}})^n = a$ and $n$ th root of $a$ is $(a^{\frac{1}{n}}) = a^{\frac{1}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{a}$

The $n$ th root of $a$ is written as $\sqrt[n]{a}$.
